review.tagline: Local Tree-sitter code graph served over MCP so agents read only affected files
review.summary: Parses a repository with Tree-sitter into a SQLite graph of functions, classes, imports, calls, inheritance and tests, then serves blast-radius and review context to AI coding tools over MCP. A single install command detects and configures about 16 tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and Zed. It also ships a GitHub Action that posts risk-scored PR comments, and updates the graph incrementally by SHA-256 hash.
review.audience: Developers using AI coding assistants on large repos who want less token use
strengths: One install command configures about 16 coding tools; uninstall leaves other config intact
Incremental re-parse by SHA-256; two-file edit on a ~3,000-file repo took about 2.5 s
Covers 30+ languages and notebooks, plus custom languages via languages.toml
Pinned-SHA benchmarks with a reproduction recipe; median 63x token reduction across 6 repos
weaknesses: Impact recall of 1.0 is circular, since ground truth comes from the same graph
Graph context can exceed a plain file read for small single-file edits
Search ranking needs work; Express queries can return no hits
Flow detection is strongest for Python and PHP/Laravel; JavaScript and Go are weaker
needs: Models: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), Google Gemini, MiniMax, Voyage AI, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
